decision_conditions: The Local Planning Authority is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities and having regard to the evidence submitted, the historic plans reviewed, publicly available information and the Council's own research, that the premises have an established lawful use as a community facility/community centre.The evidence demonstrates that the premises were historically used for community, social, educational and recreational activities and that no material change of use has subsequently occurred. Officers have further considered whether the lawful use has been abandoned and, having regard to all relevant circumstances, are not satisfied that abandonment has taken place.Accordingly, officers are satisfied that the established lawful use of the premises is as a community facility/community centre and that such use falls within Use Class F2(a) of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended). A Certificate of Lawfulness should therefore be granted pursuant to Section 191 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
